messages:
alex: Heads up — e2e perf gate failed on canary after the autoscale smoothing change. p95 jumped from ~38ms -> ~220ms during the 2k concurrent run. CI job: `e2e-canary-aws-us-west-2 #4521`
ci-bot: Job failed for e2e-canary-aws-us-west-2 #4521 — logs: https://ci.redwood.internal/job/4521 (exit code 1)
maria: @alex was that the PR that touched batcher timing? which commit?
alex: yes, landed `autoscale/smoothing` change in commit abc137 (sha: abc137def). It changed the batcher smoothing window and max_delay behavior.
sam: I triggered the job, looks reproducible. Can someone /rerun so we know it's not a transient infra fluke?
ci-bot: Rerun queued: https://ci.redwood.internal/job/4521/rerun (started)
jin: Can you paste the failing assertion or a log excerpt? I can start a git bisect if it's deterministic across CI runs.
alex: log snippet: ```
[perf] p95 latency exceeded threshold: expected < 60ms, observed 220ms
[worker] batcher.waited_for_window=180ms, batch_size=128
[serving] kv-cache hits normal
```
maria: @jin if you can bisect that would be great. Start range abc000..abc200 maybe?
jin: starting bisect across abc000..abc200 now. I'll run focused small reproducer locally then escalate to CI. ETA ~20m.
perf-bot: Quick cluster correlation: p95 spikes align with increased batching delay. Suspect `batcher.max_delay_ms` + smoothing interaction. Suggest rolling canary flag revert to mitigate.
alex: current canary config excerpt: ```json
{"batcher.max_delay_ms": 50, "auto_scale.window_s": 60, "smoothing.alpha": 0.8}
```
sam: I opened a quick revert PR to toggle smoothing off for canary: https://git.redwood/repo/pull/6789
ci-bot: Rerun #4521 completed — failed again at 1799001300 on step "throughput/load-gen".
jin: first bisect pass narrowed it to commit abc137 (same one alex mentioned). I'm running a smaller harness now to confirm root cause.
perf-bot: Ran two short canary runs with smoothing disabled; p95 back to ~42ms.
maria: Ok — let's revert the smoothing change on canary while we finish the root-cause analysis. @alex can you approve the revert?
alex: Approved and merged the canary revert flag (`canary.smoothing=false`). PR: https://git.redwood/repo/pull/6790
sam: Canary after revert — two runs show p95 40ms and 44ms. Looks stable. :thumbsup: :eyes:
jin: I'll keep running the bisect + detailed profiler to propose a fix that preserves smoothing but avoids the latency cliff.
maria: Thanks everyone. I'll file a follow-up to redesign the smoothing algorithm and add a canary test to catch this pattern. Issue: infra/serving#4872.
alex: Filing a short retrospective and linking bisect artifacts. Good catch.
note: thread contains CI rerun links, logs, and a bisect start — concise coordination and triage for a p95 perf regression on canary after autoscale change
